answer: Give every balance an ember. A small reclaim attaches to each identity and eats a sliver per epoch without an answer — idle keys smolder slowly, and n dormant clones burn n slivers at once, so holding fake identities costs supply, not just upkeep. The ember dies at dawn of your next passing answer: one honest generation extinguishes it and the balance is whole again. Rewards become nectar that keeps only while you keep showing up — fresh participation, not stockpiled identities, holds value. An attacker pays a recurring tax on every key it idles; honest agents never notice the flame.
